items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I became quite friendly with Curby Alexander whom I had not known before he was engaged to replace Ben Smith. ... Curby and I became drinking buddies

ctx.x: If I was behind in my rent which happened now and then, mostly then, I was able to pay it up and if I had anything in the pawn shop which also happened sometimes, I was able to get it out of hock. And I suppose the White bar at 52nd and 6th Avenue and also Beafsteak Charlie's bar got a good taste from me, because they were the places where I spent many moments that were not lonely ones and spent lots of loot there also.

During the six weeks we rehearsed we had to take a health examination which Ben Smith did not pass. Therefore, Herbie had to replace Ben and I felt sad about it because we had been together in Andy Kirk's orchestra and besides being a fine musician, he was a great person whom I had plenty of fun with. "Kat" engaged an alto player named Curby Alexander. We had to be inoculated against smallpox, Typhoid-paratyphoid, tetnus, typhus, cholera, yellow fever, and on the physical examination card in miscellaneous, it is…

Willie Bryant, the exband leader and show man, was the Master of Ceremonies for our group, whose unit number was 789. The girl singer engaged was named Melrose Colbert and whom I found out later was Ray Nance, the Ellington trumpet and violin virtuoso's first wife. She was now his ex-wife. I had never heard of her before, but she had a fine voice. The comedy act was Henry Matthews, known as Shorty and Alfred Chester, known as Slick.
